app.logicalOrderTitle: Logical order, not the physical plan.
app.logicalOrderNote: Stages follow the logical order SQL Server uses to define the result: FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT → DISTINCT → ORDER BY → TOP. The real engine may run operations in a different order (execution plan), but the result is the same.
app.footer: Open-source educational tool (MIT license). Data is processed only in your browser.

where.summaryUnknown_one: row is UNKNOWN (it compares with NULL).
where.summaryUnknown_other: rows are UNKNOWN (they compare with NULL).
where.summaryUnknownPart_one: row discarded because {{condition}} is UNKNOWN (it compares with NULL).
where.summaryUnknownPart_other: rows discarded because {{condition}} is UNKNOWN (they compare with NULL).

from.explanation: This is the starting point: every row and column of the table is taken, and each next stage works on them.

where.explanation: The condition is evaluated on each row. Only rows where it is true pass; those where it is false or UNKNOWN are discarded.

groupBy.explanation: Rows with the same value are put together in a group; each color (G1, G2…) is a group.
groupBy.wholeTable: There is no GROUP BY, but the query uses aggregate functions: all the rows form a single group.

aggregate.explanation: Each aggregate is computed with the rows of its group, and each group is summarized in a single row.

having.explanation: It filters groups, not rows: the condition is evaluated with the aggregates already computed. That is why SUM or COUNT can be used here but not in WHERE.

select.explanation: Aliases and expressions are only computed here; that is why they cannot be used in WHERE, GROUP BY or HAVING.
select.star: With * every column of the table is returned, in its order.

distinct.explanation: A row is a duplicate if it is equal in every column; only the first one stays.

orderBy.explanation: ASC goes from lowest to highest and DESC from highest to lowest; on a tie, the next key decides.

top.explanation: The first rows in the current order are kept; the rest are discarded.
top.percent: With PERCENT, the number is computed from the total and rounded up: {{percent}}% of {{count}} rows is $t(common.rows, {"count": {{n}} }).

result.explanation: This is what SQL Server would return.

where.unknown: {{condition}} is UNKNOWN because it compares with NULL: {{evaluated}}

having.unknown: {{condition}} is UNKNOWN because it compares with NULL: {{evaluated}}

note.unknownIsDiscarded: A comparison with NULL is neither true nor false: it is UNKNOWN, and WHERE or HAVING only let through what is true. To look for NULL values use IS NULL.
note.intDivision: {{column}} divides two integers: SQL Server drops the decimals (7 / 2 = 3). To get 3.5 write 7 / 2.0.
note.avgInt: {{aggregate}} averages integers, so SQL Server drops the decimals of the result (16 / 3 = 5). To get decimals: AVG(column * 1.0).
note.nullsIgnored_one: {{aggregate}} ignores NULLs: {{count}} NULL value was ignored.
note.nullsIgnored_other: {{aggregate}} ignores NULLs: {{count}} NULL values were ignored.
note.nullGroup: Rows with NULL in the grouping column form their own group: for GROUP BY, NULLs are equal to each other.
note.emptyGroupsNoRows: No rows reach GROUP BY, so no group is formed and the result is empty.
note.aggregateWithoutGroupBy: Without GROUP BY, a query with aggregates always returns exactly one row, even with no rows: COUNT gives 0 and SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX give NULL.
note.havingWithoutGroupBy: HAVING without GROUP BY treats the whole table as a single group.
note.caseInsensitive: With SQL Server's default collation, text is compared ignoring case: "dog" and "Dog" fall in the same group.
note.nullsSortFirst: SQL Server treats NULL as the lowest value: it comes first with ASC and last with DESC.
note.orderByHiddenColumn: Rows are sorted by {{column}}, which is not in the SELECT: ORDER BY can use table columns even if they are not shown.
note.topWithoutOrder: TOP without ORDER BY does not guarantee which rows come back: SQL Server may pick any. Here they are taken in table order.
note.distinctNulls: For DISTINCT, two NULLs are considered equal.

error.EMPTY_QUERY: The query is empty. Write a SELECT statement.
error.NOT_A_SELECT: Only SELECT queries can be visualized; {{statement}} is not supported.
error.MULTIPLE_STATEMENTS: Write one query at a time ({{count}} were found).
error.UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE: {{feature}}: not supported yet in this version.
error.MISSING_FROM: The FROM clause is missing: say which table the data comes from.
error.TABLE_NOT_FOUND: Invalid object name "{{table}}": there is no table with that name.
error.COLUMN_NOT_FOUND: Invalid column name "{{column}}": the {{table}} table has no such column.
error.INVALID_QUALIFIER: The multi-part identifier "{{qualifier}}.{{column}}" could not be bound: {{qualifier}} is not the name or alias of the table in FROM.
error.ALIAS_NOT_ALLOWED: "{{alias}}" is a SELECT alias and cannot be used in {{clause}}, because SELECT is processed later. Repeat the whole expression.
error.COLUMN_NOT_IN_GROUP_BY: Column "{{column}}" is invalid in {{clause}} because it is not in GROUP BY and not inside an aggregate function.
error.AGGREGATE_IN_WHERE: An aggregate such as {{aggregate}} cannot appear in WHERE: WHERE filters rows before grouping. To filter on an aggregate use HAVING.
error.AGGREGATE_IN_GROUP_BY: An aggregate function cannot be used in GROUP BY: {{aggregate}}.
error.NESTED_AGGREGATE: An aggregate function cannot be used inside another one: {{aggregate}}.
error.AGGREGATE_TYPE_INVALID: Operand data type {{type}} is invalid for the {{fn}} operator.
error.NON_BOOLEAN_CONDITION: {{expression}} is not a condition: a comparison was expected (for example with =, >, LIKE or IS NULL).
error.GROUP_BY_CONSTANT: Each GROUP BY expression must contain at least one column: {{expression}}.
error.ORDER_BY_POSITION_OUT_OF_RANGE: ORDER BY {{position}} is out of range: the SELECT has $t(common.columns, {"count": {{count}} }).
error.ORDER_BY_NOT_IN_SELECT_DISTINCT: With SELECT DISTINCT, ORDER BY items must appear in the select list: {{item}}.
error.CONVERSION_FAILED: Conversion failed: "{{value}}" cannot be converted to type {{type}}.
error.INVALID_TABLE_DATA: Table {{table}} has an invalid value in row {{row}}, column {{column}}: "{{value}}" is not of type $t(table.types.{{type}}).
